# 2024-604 — Quixilver: Domotron

Primary source: https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-604-quixilver-presents-our-2024-robot-cad-and-code-release/477799

Reviewed 2026-10-26. This is a source-bounded technical study. Construction, stated intent, interpretation and unresolved evidence are separate.

## 2024 release and May 2025 follow-up · intake

### Published construction or code

Polycarbonate rollers flex under impact; short dead-axle sections avoid a full-width shaft permanently bending. The team reports rollers deflecting more than half their diameter in bad hits. Deployment ties the two sides through chain and a cross shaft inside the frame.

### Stated rationale and boundaries

Compliance, weight and packaging drove the split-axle construction. The team explicitly reports axle-mount bolts shearing and deployment chain snapping, unresolved during the season.

### Engineering interpretation

A compliant roller is not the same as a robust entire intake. Moving deformation away from a long shaft can concentrate load in axle bolts or a mechanically coupled deployment system. This matters directly to 1833’s request for something beefy: copy the load path and its known limitations, not merely the visible material. The 2026 independently driven arms are a later response to the chain failure, not a configuration that existed throughout 2024.

### Validation still required

Verify the installed configuration and interfaces against the original publication/CAD; prototype full acquisition-to-output cycles, recovery and service access under the intended loaded and defended conditions. These tests are proposed, not performed.

## 2024 published CAD versus installed hardware · controls

### Published construction or code

The team says bellypan holes were hand-drilled and omitted from CAD, electronics were suppressed to reduce CAD lag, shooter shafts were actually cut shorter, and a reused climber shaft tensioned surgical tubing absent from CAD.

### Stated rationale and boundaries

Some differences were drafting omissions, some deliberate reuse and some effort-versus-benefit decisions.

### Engineering interpretation

A released CAD assembly is a valuable geometry reference but not a perfect as-built record. A long shaft in a rendering is not automatically an intended design feature. Likewise, suppressed electronics do not imply an unplanned electrical layout. Follow the team’s replies when interpreting the release. The existing interview synopsis documents the asymmetric launcher and trap system; this addition focuses on the explicitly published manufacturing and intake corrections.

### Validation still required

Verify the installed configuration and interfaces against the original publication/CAD; prototype full acquisition-to-output cycles, recovery and service access under the intended loaded and defended conditions. These tests are proposed, not performed.

## Evidence limits

- Only source-established configurations and changes are described; intermediate revisions may remain unresolved.
- Selected primary publications/code reviewed; exact per-event installation and exhaustive intermediate revisions remain unresolved.
- Four previously blocked source originals (2023 robot photo; 2026 serializer, intake and hopper CAD views) were recovered through normal browser downloads on 2026-10-26 and inspected. Whole-robot source views are not exhaustive mechanism or event-version certification.

# 2024-604: Controlled centering preserves deliberately asymmetric shooting contact

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

A wide compliant/dead-axis intake and guides center the note before an asymmetric launcher contact sequence. The same scoring assembly handles amp delivery and rises for trap work. Beam-break acquisition feedback retracts the collector and rumbles the driver controller.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team identifies driver tolerance, source pickup speed and long-range scoring that reduces driving as priorities. The source reports about a second of cycle improvement from acquisition feedback/retraction behavior; that is a team estimate, not an isolated controlled trial.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

Ring deformation and lateral offset can change which launcher contact happens first. Centering is therefore part of generating the intended spin, not merely getting the note somewhere inside the robot. The driver-feedback example also shows how a small state signal can reduce wasted acquisition motion without changing motor power.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Vary lateral entry, note wear and intake speed; measure spin, trajectory spread and complete cycle time. Separate the effect of a wider pickup from the effect of better feedback.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.

source_reviews.title: Domotron CAD and code release
facts: Polycarbonate intake roller can flex on impact. Short axle pieces replaced a continuous shaft. Chain and an inboard cross shaft tie the deployment sides together.
The team reports sheared axle-mount bolts and broken deployment chain, unresolved in-season.
Installed electronics, shafts, bellypan drillings and climber assist differed from the visible CAD.
source_reviews.limitations: Team account supplies failure types but gives no frequency or force measurements.

source_reviews.title: FRC604 public code
facts: FRC-2024 is labeled end-of-Champs. FRC-2024-NEW includes offseason changes and dependency updates.
source_reviews.limitations: No Java execution or deployment reconstruction.

source_reviews.title: Domotron Behind the Bumpers
facts: The older study describes an asymmetric launcher and separate trap handling.

source_review.whole_robot_explanation: Domotron used a collector designed to deform and recover when struck. In the team's account, a full-width hex shaft would have bent permanently under impacts that the roller tube itself could survive. The design therefore separates the roller's local axle supports from the cross-robot synchronization path. The observed failures show where durability moved next. Both the bolts at the roller supports and the chain in the deployment mechanism remained vulnerable. The public release is unusually explicit about the differences between the assembly drawing and the machine the team actually serviced.
piece_flow: The compliant collector pulls a floor note into the protected feed area described in the older dossier.
The inherited path stages the note for the asymmetric launcher or the separate endgame delivery mechanism. The release discussion does not specify the complete routing sequence.
source_review.packaging_and_motion: The pickup's rigid cross shaft sits inside the frame while the roller spans the exposed mouth. That frees the outer roller to bow without relying on a long shaft. Ensure the bow envelope clears the bumper and internal rollers, and check whether a bent or partially displaced roller can retract. At the upper mechanism, use the as-built shaft length and actual surgical tubing when checking clearance, not the release image alone.

subsystems.name: Compliant intake rollers
subsystems.construction: Polycarbonate tube, short end axle segments, tube plugs and bolted side supports. Later supports used purchased 3/8-inch OD spacers.
subsystems.operation: Roll to acquire while elastically deflecting during a hit.
subsystems.team_rationale: The team wanted resilience and low weight. Small bearings fit the plugs and later spacers avoided cutting hex stock.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: The tube can survive an impact that yields a shaft, but the constraint forces still pass into the axle bolts and side plates. Larger bolts could shift failure into the plug or mount.
subsystems.interfaces: Axial retention, tube clearance, side plate spacing and replaceable roller ends.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Axle bolts sheared in use. Compare change time, repeat alignment and whether an impact can pull the plug out of the tube.
subsystems.unknowns: Wall thickness, bolt grade, actual peak deflection and frequency.

subsystems.name: Deployment and chassis
subsystems.construction: Chain and an in-frame cross shaft mechanically link left and right.
subsystems.operation: Deploy and retract both sides together.
subsystems.team_rationale: A cross link ties the sides without needing a rigid crossbar in the exposed collector.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: An offset collision can drive load into both sides of the linkage. Once the chain breaks, an otherwise intact roller may leave the whole intake out of position.
subsystems.interfaces: Timing, travel stops and slack need to tolerate asymmetric load and ordinary wear.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Chain snapping occurred during the season. Proposed check: hit one side at an angle and try to stow before realigning it.
subsystems.unknowns: Chain load and whether a sacrificial coupling or alternate drive would maintain useful recovery.

subsystems.name: Elevator, shooter and service
subsystems.construction: Older dossier describes asymmetric launch and trap hardware. The release confirms elevator shaft reuse for surgical tubing and shortened actual shooter shafts.
subsystems.operation: Move the scorer and operate the chain assist without contacting nearby structure.
subsystems.team_rationale: The team reused available hardware and suppressed electronics in CAD for performance.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: A visible shaft may be an obsolete design remnant or a useful assist mounting point. A service plan needs the actual machine and wiring view.
subsystems.interfaces: Verify tubing travel, shaft clearance and access to the drill pattern and electronics.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Compare release geometry to actual repairs and hardware before deriving clearances or spares.
subsystems.unknowns: Event-specific wire routing, shot settings and complete feed sequence.

revisions: Team confirmed spacer substitution, shorter installed shooter shafts and reuse from an earlier climber. The repository separates end-of-Champs and offseason software.
transferable_principles: Trace impact loads beyond the flexible part and check whether the robot can still stow after failure. Release CAD and pit configuration should be reconciled before copying.
disconfirming_conditions: The flex design loses its advantage if it causes roller-to-frame contact or an unrecoverable deployment-chain failure. A stiffer assembly may be preferable when replaceable supports can absorb impacts at lower repair cost.
remaining_gaps: Championship state logic, installed geometry at the note handoff and fault-rate measurements.
recommended_images: Release post 3 electronics layout and climber assist images
Intake roller plug and protected cross-shaft view
